definition: A separate, typically smaller model used specifically to check the inputs or outputs of a primary model against safety or policy constraints.
details: Guardrail models offload safety-related classification from the main generative model, allowing dedicated, often faster and more specialized filtering as part of a layered safety architecture.

explainer.lead: A guardrail model is a dedicated safety checker that sits alongside a primary AI model. It examines prompts or generated answers so the main model can focus on its task while specialized filtering handles policy and safety decisions.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a shop with a person who makes things and a separate checker who makes sure each order and finished item follows the rules. The checker is usually smaller and quicker, and can stop a request or answer before it goes any further. This gives the shop more than one chance to catch a problem.
tiers.practitioner: Deploy a guardrail model as a separate classification stage before generation, after generation, or both. Its decisions can allow, block, or route content for further handling, while the primary model remains responsible for generation. A key pitfall is treating this single layer as the complete safety architecture rather than one specialized filter within it.
tiers.paperLevel: Let M be the primary generative model and G a separate guardrail model: G evaluates an input x, an output y, or both against safety or policy constraints and returns a filtering decision. This separates safety classification from generation and permits a smaller, faster, more specialized G. Its coverage is limited to the checks and placement chosen for that layer.

explainer.example: A user sends a chatbot a prompt that violates its safety policy. An input guardrail model flags the prompt, so the primary model is not asked to generate an answer and the user receives a refusal instead; for an allowed prompt, a second check can inspect the generated answer before it is displayed.

usedIn.name: Generative AI applications
usedIn.detail: Checks user prompts or model answers before they are accepted or shown.

usedIn.name: Layered safety systems
usedIn.detail: Provides a dedicated filtering layer alongside the primary generative model.

explainer.intuition: Think of a specialist inspector working beside a general-purpose producer: the producer handles the main task, while the inspector concentrates only on whether a request or result breaks the rules. Separating these jobs allows safety checks to be faster and more specialized.
howItWorks: A user prompt arrives at the primary model's input path.
A guardrail model can classify the prompt against safety or policy constraints.
If the prompt passes, the primary model generates a response.
The same or another guardrail model can check that response.
The system releases the response only if the applicable checks allow it.
explainer.whyItMatters: Guardrail models move safety classification out of the main generative model and into a dedicated component. This supports specialized, often faster filtering and makes the checks one layer in a broader safety architecture.
misconceptions: A guardrail model is not the primary model generating the answer.
It need not check only outputs; it can check inputs, outputs, or both.
It is one safety layer, not a guarantee that every unsafe result will be caught.

diagram.caption: Dedicated guardrail models can filter both the prompt and the primary model's generated response.
